answer: PPAP (Production Part Approval Process) is the automotive-industry framework in which a supplier proves to a customer that a part, as actually produced with production tooling and at production rate, meets every drawing/specification/quality requirement before mass shipment — by submitting a defined document package (PSW form, dimensional results, material and performance test reports, process capability studies, etc.) at the customer's chosen submission level (1–5). In practice it is the launch gate: the customer reviews and signs (or rejects/interim-rejects) the PSW, and only after approval can the part go into series production, so any open issue at that point triggers corrective action and resubmission. One note: I searched our readable company materials for a PPAP-specific internal standard and found nothing in that scope, so the above is general industry practice rather than a documented house rule.
